draft.title: Origins of the Cold War
card: The United States and the Soviet Union were allies against Nazi Germany in the Second World War. After 1945 their wartime partnership gave way to distrust.
They disagreed about politics and economics. The United States backed democracy and capitalism. The Soviet Union was a one-party communist state with a state-run economy.

They also disagreed about Europe's future. Soviet forces stayed in much of Eastern Europe, and communist governments came to power there. The United States and its allies saw this as Soviet expansion, while the Soviet Union saw it as protection against future invasion.

Europe divided into a Western bloc, linked to the United States, and a Soviet bloc in the east. Each side feared the other's aims, so the Cold War was a state of tension and rivalry that stopped short of open war between them.
draft.remember: Wartime allies became rivals after 1945 as mutual fear and a divided Europe hardened.

a.q: Which best explains why the United States and the Soviet Union became rivals after 1945?
opts: The war against Germany ended and deep differences showed
Each side blamed the other for starting the war in Europe
The Soviet Union left the alliance before Germany fell
The two powers fought a direct war over Eastern Europe
a.why: The alliance was held together by the war against Germany. Once that ended, differences in politics, economics and plans for Europe produced distrust. Open war between them did not occur, so the last option is wrong.
a.clue: Think about what had joined the two powers together.

b.q: Soviet forces remained in Poland after 1945 and a communist government took power there. How did the two sides most likely interpret this?
opts: The West saw expansion, while the Soviet Union saw security
Both sides saw it as a step towards lasting friendship
The West saw security, while the Soviet Union saw expansion
Both sides agreed it was an internal Polish matter
b.why: Western leaders feared the spread of Soviet power and communism. The Soviet Union argued that friendly governments on its border protected it from invasion. The reverse reading has the two views the wrong way round.
b.clue: Each side read the same event through its own fears.

a.best: The war against Germany ended and deep differences showed

b.best: The West saw expansion, while the Soviet Union saw security

problems.detail: Why (a) says 'Open war between them did not occur, so the last option is wrong', but options are shown in random order, and the direct-war option is not the last one here. As written, the why points students at 'The Soviet Union left the alliance before Germany fell'. It should name the direct-war option by its content, not its position.
